[ASSISTANT_SAID] To convert a date string in cell B3 to epoch time and then to GMT-5, use the formula: `=(((B3-(5/24))-DATE(1899,12,30))*86400)`  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The formula will give the number of seconds elapsed since the epoch (12/30/1899 12:00 AM) in GMT-5.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To convert this number back to a date string in GMT-5, use the formula: `=TEXT((((B3-(5/24))-DATE(1899,12,30))*86400)/86400+DATE(1899,12,30),"MM/DD/YYYY hh:mm:ss AM/PM")`  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The result of the second formula should be: `01/17/2023 12:26:31 PM`.  
[USER] Asked why the number of seconds is calculated since December 30, 1899, and not January 1, 1970.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Explained that January 1, 1970, is the epoch time used in modern computer systems, while Excel uses December 30, 1899, as its reference point for computing time.  
[USER] Asked if the two formulas can be combined into one.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Confirmed that they can be combined into a single formula: `=TEXT((((B3-(5/24))-DATE(1899,12,30))*86400)/86400+DATE(1899,12,30),"MM/DD/YYYY hh:mm:ss AM/PM")`  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The result of the combined formula should be: `01/17/2023 12:26:31 PM`.

[USER] Provided an example with cell B2 showing `1/17/2023 1:26:31 PM` and the formula result as `01/17/2023 08:26:31 AM`.
